summary.text: 半 means “half.” A reported bronze-form analysis reads 八 as division and 牛 as the ox being divided. One account proposes that “half” developed from “split/open”; another explicitly treats “half” as the original meaning. The evidence does not settle their competing accounts.

formation.text: A reported bronze-form analysis treats 半 as a compound: 八 marks division and is also proposed as a sound element; 牛 depicts the ox being divided. The cited Old Chinese forms share an initial but differ in their endings, so they do not establish 八’s proposed sound role.

components.text: In the reported bronze-form analysis, 八 marks division and is also assigned a sound role. The Old Chinese forms share an initial but have different endings, so the comparison permits a possible sound link without establishing it.

sound.text: In the Baxter–Sagart system, the forms share an initial but have different endings. This is compatible with a sound relation but does not establish 八’s role in 半.
These current Mandarin readings are distinct and do not establish 八’s proposed historical sound role in 半.

components.text: 牛 depicts the ox understood as the object being divided in this analysis.

history.text: Bronze and Small Seal forms of 半 are recorded, including a bronze example and the received Shuowen form. The records support these form types but do not establish a complete sequence of graphic changes.

半 is reported as a spelling for 磐 in a Mawangdui Zhouyi manuscript where the received text has 磐桓. Reconstructions suggest similar labial onsets and -an material, but come from different systems and do not establish the manuscript token’s sound or the scribe’s reason for choosing 半.

uncertainties.text: Two proposals give different starting points: “split/open” may have developed into “half,” or “half” may have been the original meaning. The available evidence does not date a transition or resolve these alternatives. The reading and date of the cited bronze occurrence remain uncertain.
八’s proposed phonetic role remains uncertain: the cited Old Chinese forms share an initial but have different, unexplained endings.
Uses meaning midpoint, partial or incomplete, and “very little” are documented, but their chronology and paths of development are unresolved.

The proposed sound basis for writing 磐 with 半 is unproven. Reconstructions from different systems suggest some labial and -an similarity, but do not establish the manuscript token’s pronunciation or the scribe’s motivation.

senses.gloss: 磐, in a reported manuscript spelling
senses.text: 半 is reported in a Mawangdui Zhouyi manuscript where the received text has 磐桓. The proposed borrowing mechanism is that 半 stood for 磐 because their spoken forms sounded alike or similarly. Reconstructions suggest similar labial onsets and -an material, but come from different systems and do not establish the manuscript token’s sound or the reason for the spelling. This is graph reuse, not a meaning of 半.

limitations.text: The proposed starting points conflict: “split/open” may have developed into “half,” or “half” may have been original. A separate proposal derives “middle” and “incomplete” from dividing an object; it does not establish that either developed from the lexical sense “half.” No dated sequence or half-to-midpoint/partial lexical path is established. Historical examples document midpoint, partial or incomplete, and “very little,” but do not establish chronological links among these meanings.
The reported spelling of 磐 with 半 is a proposed whole-graph sound loan. The manuscript wording and the sound match between 半 and 磐 remain uncertain.

overview.text: 半 means ‘half.’ In one reported bronze-form analysis, 八 marks division and 牛 depicts the ox being divided. The proposed sound role for 八 and the competing accounts of whether “split/open” or “half” came first remain unsettled.

limitations.text: The cited bronze example is identified in paleographic records, but its specific inscription image has not been verified against a primary transcription or artifact image. The available seal-script redraw also does not clearly show the reported 八-and-牛 structure, so no candidate reliably illustrates the character’s historical shape or the proposed component analysis.
